analysis.title: Investment Weekly - 20 November 2026
key_insights: Brent fell from nearly USD120 in early November to about USD90, with consensus at USD80 next year, yet 2026's rise in 10-year yields came from real yields, not breakevens, which stayed flat.
Cheaper energy rarely lowers real yields unless demand collapses. It supports real incomes and resilient US growth, keeping modest Fed hikes on the table amid sticky core inflation.
Heavy debt supply keeps real yields high. Record US IG issuance this year was driven by big tech, with cloud giants projected to borrow another USD300-400bn in 2027.

If yields stay elevated in 2027, bonds offer meaningful income but may cushion equity drawdowns unevenly, and high real yields cap equity valuations. HSBC favours rotating from US mega-caps into healthcare, staples, Europe and India.

AI is producing rolling 'baby bubbles' across software, silver and semiconductors. Cheap, unloved healthcare is seen as the next candidate, with 2027 consensus profit growth cooling in most sectors while healthcare accelerates.

Fed chair Warsh flagged AI sustaining substantially higher US growth without inflation. OECD estimates AI could add 0.8-1.3pp to annual G7 productivity growth over a decade. HSBC's 'Productivity miracle' upside case has US growth at 3%.

Ramp data show US firm AI token usage up over 80% since July with spend flat, as token prices halved on a price war led by Chinese models. This raises doubts on hyperscaler monetisation and argues against US mega-cap concentration.

Renminbi bonds are pitched as a diversifier: low inflation, supportive policy, light foreign ownership, offshore CNH up nearly 5% vs USD this year, and about RMB6tn of hidden local debt swapped into transparent bonds.

Global equities sold off broadly, with the S&P 500 on track for its worst week since early Q2 2025. Taiwan TAIEX fell 17.5% and KOSPI 7.9% on the week, while India rose 2.2%. DXY hit its highest since April 2025 and gold fell below $3,600.

October FOMC minutes showed almost all participants judged further rate hikes likely appropriate, and Waller said the Fed must be a little more aggressive. HSBC expects modest curve steepening and less tightening than priced.
House view: cautiously pro-risk, preferring Asia and EM growth. It favours quality in credit, sees US 10-year yields range-bound near term, and likes hedge funds (macro and CTA) as bond alternatives.
Week ahead: flash PMIs, Conference Board confidence, October PCE (forecast 3.8% yoy), Q3 GDP second estimate (3.4%), and a Bank of Korea hike expected to 3.25%.

earnings_insights: US/European Q3 results 95% complete with beats in energy, staples, tech and healthcare. Consensus 2026e EPS growth is 35% for the US and 23% for Europe (estimates).
Consensus forecasts show 2027 profit growth cooling across almost every sector while healthcare accelerates (estimate).

tension_points.bull_case: Falling Brent toward USD80 should cool inflation and pull Treasury yields lower.
tension_points.bear_case: Real yields drove the rise, cheaper energy supports real incomes and growth, and heavy debt supply keeps real yields high.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Demand collapse would lower real yields.

tension_points.bull_case: Software playbook of low prices, embedding AI, then raising fees, plus productivity gains.
tension_points.bear_case: Token prices halved, easy model switching prevents lock-in, and each query burns costly chips and power.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Rising revenue from booming usage would ease monetisation doubts.
